why_intro: A new, independent blockchain, created in 2026, with no mining: the LockKeepers' computers check, accept and record every transfer. No name or personal data — each account is just an address — and several protections so you don't lose your money or make mistakes when sending or receiving.

why.title: Mistakes are undone
why.body: Every transfer waits up to 1 hour for the recipient to accept it. If they don't, the coins come back to you, and you can cancel while it waits. Coins only go to registered accounts, and every address carries a check: a typo is refused.

why.title: Theft is stopped
why.body: "It wasn't me" freezes your account in one tap and cancels what is waiting. A second phone can be required for new contacts or large amounts. Daily limits, a send code and fingerprint add more locks.

why.title: Nothing is lost forever
why.body: Your heirs receive your coins if you are gone. Trusted people can move your coins to a new wallet if you lose your 24 words. The Sovereign Vault makes every sending wait the days you choose.

why.title: A fixed, fair supply
why.body: Only 40,000,000 LOCK will ever exist: 1,000 at the start to run the network, 400,000 (1%) for the creator, and the rest released over 30 years, halving every 5 years. Nobody can create more, and these rules cannot be changed. After the 30 years, 800,000 LOCK kept apart (2%) keep going to the LockKeepers, half of what is left every 30 years: 99.9% by year 330 and the last LOCK around the year 3466.

why.title: How new coins are released
why.body: New LOCK appear with every block, about once every 5 seconds. Every hour they are shared among all LockKeepers that were switched on, by hours on and the LOCK they have in guarantee.

why.title: Fast and cheap
why.body: A new block about every 5 seconds, and a transfer is final at once. The fee is 0.1% (at least 0.0002, at most 0.01 LOCK) and you see it before sending. Registering, accepting and cancelling are free.

why.title: Ready for quantum computers
why.body: Every account signs with two keys at once: a classic one and a post-quantum one (ML-DSA-65). Your wallet is encrypted on your device with your password and the phone's security chip.

why.title: Only real computers keep the network
why.body: Every LockKeeper is a real computer, confirmed by the security chip it has from the factory. One computer is one LockKeeper and one vote: cloud servers and virtual machines are refused. So nobody can fill the network with fake computers to take control of it.

why.title: Nobody owns it
why.body: No company controls the network and no vote can change its golden rules. Your wallet is yours alone: only your 24 words open it.

lk_body: The EncryptLock network has no owner. It runs on computers called LockKeepers, run by different people. Each keeps a copy of all accounts and checks every transfer; a group drawn by lot among those switched on, always changing, signs a new block about every 5 seconds. To be a LockKeeper you put at least 1 dollar of LOCK in guarantee, and it stays yours. Switching off costs nothing: you just don't earn while off. Only cheating loses part of the guarantee. Every hour the new coins and part of the fees are shared among all LockKeepers that were on, by hours on and guarantee, straight into the balance. None can get more than 5%. Each LockKeeper is a real computer, confirmed by its factory security chip: one computer, one LockKeeper.
earn_title: Help the blockchain: be a LockKeeper with your computer
earn_body: Help run the EncryptLock blockchain and earn LOCK. On your computer, go to encryptlock.pages.dev and download EncryptLock for PC. It uses very little power, does no mining and only checks and records transfers. The more hours it is on, the more you earn.
chain_intro: A shared record book that nobody owns, kept by many computers at once. These are its rules.

chain.title: A shared record book
chain.body: Every account and transfer is written in blocks, about one every 5 seconds. Every LockKeeper keeps a full copy and checks each transfer: the signatures must be the owner's and the coins must exist. A transfer is final as soon as its block is signed.

chain.title: A fixed amount
chain.body: Only 40,000,000 LOCK will ever exist: 1,000 at the start to run the network, 400,000 (1%) for the creator, and the rest released over 30 years. The amount released halves every 5 years. Nobody can create more. After the 30 years, 800,000 LOCK kept apart (2%) keep going to the LockKeepers, half of what is left every 30 years: 99.9% by year 330 and the last LOCK around the year 3466.

chain.title: LockKeepers
chain.body: The computers that keep the network running. Anyone can run one. The guarantee is at least 1 dollar of LOCK (at the price of the last trade), and it is not a payment: nobody receives it, not the founder, not the blockchain. The LOCK stay in the person's own account, only locked, and keep being theirs. Whoever has no LOCK buys them in Buy / Sell from whoever is selling (the USDC go to that seller). To stop, the person asks for the guarantee back and the LOCK are free 21 days later. Only cheating costs part of it. Each LockKeeper is a real computer, confirmed by its factory security chip: one computer, one LockKeeper.

chain.title: Who signs the blocks
chain.body: Each block is signed by a group drawn by lot among the LockKeepers switched on without a break for at least 1 hour. Everyone has the same chance and, inside the group, each computer is one vote: the guarantee counts for the earnings, not for signing. The group starts with 100 and grows with the network up to 300. It changes a little at a time (about 10% per hour) so everyone gets a turn, and anyone who stops signing for about 5 minutes is replaced at once. With fewer than 100 switched on, all of them sign. At the start, while there are fewer than 20 stable LockKeepers (100 hours on in 7 days), the computer that started the network holds more than 2/3 of the power to sign, so a computer switched off never stops the network; from 20 on, every computer counts the same.

chain.title: Who earns
chain.body: Everyone switched on, not only those signing. Every hour the new coins and the LockKeepers' share of the fees are shared by hours on × guarantee. The more LockKeepers are on, the smaller each share. Nobody can get more than 5%.

chain.title: Switching off costs nothing
chain.body: A LockKeeper that switches off loses neither its guarantee nor what it has earned: it just doesn't earn while off, and comes back by itself when switched on again. Only cheating costs something: signing two different blocks burns 5% of the guarantee, and saying it is on without working earns nothing for that time.

chain.title: Fees
chain.body: Transfers: 0.1% paid by the sender (minimum 0.0002, maximum 0.01 LOCK). Trades between LOCK and USDC: 0.25% paid by the seller. Registering, accepting and cancelling are free. Fees are split between the development fund and the LockKeepers: 75/25 in the first 5 years, then 50/50 for ever (sooner if the network reaches 10 million active wallets).

chain.title: Golden rules nobody can change
chain.body: The fixed amount, the release over 30 years, the 5% limit, the protections of every account and the fee split are built into the network itself. No vote and no company can change them. The everlasting reserve for the LockKeepers too.

chain.title: Public code, view only
chain.body: EncryptLock's code is public on GitHub (encryptlock-codigo): anyone can read it and check that these rules are really there. It is view-only, forever: nobody may copy it, change it or launch another network with it.

chain.title: It depends on nobody
chain.body: As long as there are LockKeepers switched on, the network keeps working, even without the founder or the first computers.

howto.title: Your wallet
howto.body: At the top, the ring of coins: swipe sideways and the coin in front is the active one. Below it: your balance, its value in €/$ once there is a market price, coins locked until a date, and whether you are connected to the network.

howto.title: Receive
howto.body: Show your QR code or copy your address. The other person reads it in EncryptLock (Send → QR icon) or with the phone's camera. The coins appear in "To accept": tap Accept within 1 hour.

howto.title: Send
howto.body: Type, paste or scan the address and enter the amount. The fee and the total appear before you confirm. The recipient has 1 hour to accept; until then you can tap Cancel and the coins come back (the fee does not).

howto.title: To accept · Sent, waiting
howto.body: Transfers coming to you show a countdown and an Accept button. The ones you sent show the time left and a Cancel button.

howto.title: The ⋮ menu
howto.body: At the top right: Settings, language, and Lock, which closes the wallet; your password opens it again.

howto.title: Password and pauses
howto.body: Your password encrypts the wallet on this device. After 5 wrong passwords you wait 2 minutes, after 10 you wait 4, and the wait keeps doubling. Forgot it? Recover the wallet with your 24 words. Settings → Change password.

howto.title: Your 24 words
howto.body: The only key to your wallet. Write them on paper and keep them safe; never photograph or share them. Settings → See the 24 words (asks for your password).

howto.title: Fingerprint / face
howto.body: On the phone: open the wallet with your finger or face. Settings → Fingerprint / face.

howto.title: Send code
howto.body: An extra code of 4 to 8 digits asked before every sending, different from your password. Settings → Send code.

howto.title: Lock when not in use
howto.body: The wallet locks itself after 1, 2, 5 or 15 minutes without being touched, and when you leave the app. Settings → Lock when not in use.

howto.title: It wasn't me
howto.body: If something was sent without you, or your phone was taken: Settings → It wasn't me. The account freezes at once and transfers waiting are cancelled. Unfreezing with only this phone takes 7 days.

howto.title: Second device
howto.body: Link another phone that can only approve and freeze, never send. It must approve sendings to new contacts or above your limit. Settings → Second device.

howto.title: Daily limit
howto.body: The most you can send in 24 hours, and the amount above which the second device must approve. Lowering applies at once; raising takes 48 hours. Settings → Daily limit.

howto.title: Alerts
howto.body: Notifications when coins leave your account, when coins wait for you, when a protected account needs approval, and when someone asks for your coins. Settings → Alerts.

howto.title: Protect another account
howto.body: On your second phone: add the account it protects. Its sendings that need approval appear on the Wallet screen, with Approve and "It wasn't me".

howto.title: Inheritance and "I'm here"
howto.body: Choose your heirs and their shares, and how long without a sign of life (at least 1 year). Any transaction, or the "I'm here" button, is a sign of life. Settings → Inheritance. If you were a LockKeeper, your guarantee goes too; anything that reaches the old account later follows on its own.

howto.title: Trusted people
howto.body: People who can move your coins to a new wallet of yours if you lose your 24 words: at least 2 must approve, then 30 days in which you can cancel. Settings → Trusted people.

howto.title: Sovereign Vault and locks
howto.body: Make every sending wait 7 to 365 days, or lock coins until a date so that nobody can move them, not even you. Settings → Sovereign Vault.

howto.title: Help someone else
howto.body: If you are someone's heir or trusted person: ask for their inheritance, or approve moving their coins to their new wallet. Settings → Help someone else.

howto.title: Become a LockKeeper
howto.body: Run the LockKeeper program on a computer with internet, for as many hours as you like: the more hours on, the more you earn, and switching off costs nothing. You need at least 1 dollar of LOCK in guarantee, and it stays yours. A phone cannot be a LockKeeper. Only real computers count: the computer proves it with the security chip it has from the factory (TPM 2.0, standard on Windows 11 computers), and each computer can be only one LockKeeper. Cloud servers and virtual machines are not accepted. Your earnings go into your balance every hour. Chip not accepted? Turn TPM on in the BIOS ("Intel PTT" or "AMD fTPM"), or use the same wallet on another computer: the guarantee goes with it.

howto.title: Network (advanced)
howto.body: The LockKeeper this app talks to. Normally you never change it. Settings → Advanced.

howto.title: Delete wallet from this device
howto.body: Removes the wallet from this device only. Your coins stay on the network and come back with your 24 words. Settings → Delete wallet.

about_body: EncryptLock is a new, independent blockchain, created in 2026. It works without mining and without wasting huge amounts of energy: transfers are checked, recorded and stored by the computers of the blockchain's LockKeepers — people all over the world who leave their computer on and receive LOCK for that work. Every one of those computers keeps a full copy of the record, so once launched the network depends on no one and cannot be switched off. It was built with several protections so people do not lose their money or make mistakes when sending or receiving: transfers that wait to be accepted, "It wasn't me", a second device, inheritance and the Sovereign Vault. The amount is fixed: only 40,000,000 LOCK will ever exist, released over 30 years, and nobody can create more. After the 30 years, a reserve of 800,000 LOCK keeps rewarding the LockKeepers for about 1,440 years.
